applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BLEU (Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union) network of over 100 bilateral investment treaties (e.g., BLEU-Hong Kong BIT, BLEU-China BIT)
More than 80 double taxation avoidance agreements (DTAAs), including Luxembourg-Germany, Luxembourg-France, Luxembourg-Netherlands, Luxembourg-United States and Luxembourg-UAE

EU trade and investment agreements (e.g., EU-Canada CETA, EU-Japan EPA, EU-Vietnam IPA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Luxembourg AML/CFT framework: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (including the Law of 25 July 2023); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and Grand-Ducal Regulation of 31 May 2019; CSSF Regulation 20-05 of 17 December 2020; Law of 19 December 2020 on the freezing of funds; Law of 23 July 2016 on the Societe en Commandite Speciale (SCSp).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (RBE is not public; post-CJEU C-37/20 access is limited to Luxembourg competent authorities, the FIU, obliged entities under AML/CFT law and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: SCSp partnership agreement and founding deed (contrat de societe)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary if notarized, or partners by private deed with certified signatures; notarial deed is mandatory where real property is contributed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (applies to foreign powers of attorney authorizing signature; the POA itself must be apostilled or legalized)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and certificate of incorporation of the corporate General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the country of incorporation (Luxembourg RCS if the GP is a Luxembourg entity)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified passport or identity document copies of each natural-person UBO and general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary, competent national authority or consulate in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing Luxembourg incorporation counsel and service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of origin of the UBO or general partner

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming account relationships and source of funds of UBOs and general partners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Credit institution of the UBO or partner in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization where required by the notary or receiving bank; original banker's signature may suffice

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of non-confusion (certificat de non-confusion) for the proposed company name
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic issuance by the RCS; presented directly to the Luxembourg notary; no apostille required

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales, as amended by the Law of 12 July 2013 introducing the special limited partnership (Société en Commandite Spéciale, SCSp); relevant provisions on commercial partnerships and the SCSp, including Articles 1, 100-108 and the SCSp provisions inserted in 2013.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 6 Avenue Guillaume, L-1650 Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif / contrat de société (partnership agreement or constitutive deed) filed with the RCS for registration and publication
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum statutory capital; no escrow or blocked account requirement. Contributions may be in cash, in kind, or by promise to contribute, as freely set out in the partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the special limited partnership (SCSp) be constituted with partnership interests subscribed by the founding partners in accordance with the constitutive deed. RESOLVED FURTHER: that the registered office of the partnership be established at [address], Luxembourg, which is approved as the official seat for legal, tax and regulatory filings. RESOLVED FURTHER: that [Name] be appointed as manager (associé gérant) with full power to represent the partnership, open financial accounts, engage professional advisors and execute filings with the Luxembourg Business Registers, the Administration des contributions directes and other competent authorities. RESOLVED FURTHER: that all ordinary administrative acts necessary for the commencement of the platform's activities are hereby authorised.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name availability and RCS conformity check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS online name-check and eRequest portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Query the LBR/RCS online portal to confirm that the proposed SCSp name is available and not confusingly similar to an existing registered name. The name must contain or be followed by the words 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale'. If desired, request a name reservation prior to deed execution.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name including SCSp designation
Statement of corporate object
Identity document of the applicant or founding partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS objects on grounds of similarity or misleading character, file a revised name request with a distinctive additional element, or submit a written objection with a reasoned explanation to the RCS within 15 calendar days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and approval of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary or legal counsel; notarization mandatory only if the contributions include immovable property
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the constitutive deed or private partnership agreement in French, German or English. Include: corporate name, registered office in Luxembourg, corporate object limited to lawful activities, duration, contribution schedule, classes of partnership interests, rights and powers of general and limited partners, manager appointment, decision-making rules, accounting and liquidation clauses. Ensure that e-sports community platform and tournament software-services activities are described in the corporate object.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement
Statement of subscriptions and contributions
Declaration of acceptance by the proposed manager
Notarial or legal due-diligence opinion if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS later rejects a clause as incompatible with public policy or mandatory Luxembourg law, execute a supplemental deed (avenant) or rectification deed signed by the partners before the competent notary or in private form, and refile the corrected instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the constitutive deed and partner subscriptions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (notaire) or, where permitted, private signature by all partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange execution of the constitutive deed before a Luxembourg notary if authentic form is used, or sign private deed counterparts. All general and limited partners must subscribe to their respective partnership interests. If notary appointed, obtain certified notarial copies (expéditions) for filing.
required_dossiers: Passport or official identity documents of all partners
Original partnership agreement
Contribution statement and payment proof for cash contributions
Consent letter from the provider of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If execution is defective, the notary or the partners may sign a correcting deed; any related fees are borne by the instructing party, and a corrected copy is submitted to the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - RCS eRegistration portal (lbr.lu) or physical counter of the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the constitutive deed and supporting appendices through the LBR eRegistration service. Complete the standard filing form, identify the managing partner, and pay the applicable registration fee. The RCS will allocate an RCS number and issue the official registration extract. The formation is effective upon compliance with filing and publication requirements.
required_dossiers: Executed constitutive deed or notarial transcript
Registered office consent letter
List of managers with powers of representation
Declaration of non-bankruptcy or non-disqualification signed by the manager
Proof of payment of RCS filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a rejection notice (bordereau de rejet), the deficiencies are corrected and the file resubmitted via eRegistration within 10 working days. If the deadline is missed, a new filing is required with re-executed signatures where applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration identification and ancillary administrative filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers; Administration des contributions directes; Administration de l'enregistrement et des domaines; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the RCS registration to obtain the Luxembourg national business identification number (matricule). Register for corporate income tax and municipal business tax with the Administration des contributions directes. If taxable supplies are made in Luxembourg, apply for a Luxembourg VAT number. Affiliate to social security where a manager or staff are employed.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Identification number activation request
Tax registration questionnaires (corporate income tax and VAT if applicable)
Social security affiliation form if the manager or employees are remunerated through Luxembourg payroll
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the matricule is delayed, request activation directly through the LBR customer service. Tax registration appeals or corrections are made in writing to the Administration des contributions directes within three months of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - ISIC 5820 (software publishing and digital e-sports community platform) is a non-industrial activity and is not subject to an industrial establishment permit under Luxembourg law. If a physical office or esports venue is later opened, the Ministry of Economy's establishment licensing directorate may become relevant.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required - no sector-specific operating permit applies to the online matchmaking and tournament platform under Luxembourg law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement - Luxembourg Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no classée facility and no environmental impact assessment required; pure software and digital platform activity has no classified installation under Luxembourg environmental law.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, volatile organic compound emissions or regulated point-source emissions. Applicable obligations are limited to proper disposal of office and information-technology waste under Luxembourg waste legislation and compliance with general municipal wastewater standards for the premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for the digital-only formation stage. If physical premises are subsequently established, the workplace clearance of the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) and fire-safety approval of the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) must be obtained for the relevant office premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; unified filing portal: MyGuichet.lu (guichet.lu); RCS registration through the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute private deed for the SCSp (no notary mandatory unless real estate contribution) and register with the RCS via MyGuichet.lu to obtain the business registration number (numéro d'immatriculation RCS), which is the primary tax identification number for the entity. Step 2: File the VAT registration application (formulaire 731) with the AEDT through MyGuichet.lu; the AEDT issues a Luxembourg VAT identification number bearing the 'LU' prefix. Step 3: For corporate/partnership income tax, the ACD assigns a matricule (national registration number) and a tax file to the SCSp; the fiscally transparent partners report their proportionate shares in their own filings. Step 4: Non-established foreign operators of B2C electronic services may alternatively register via the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) in their Member State of identification; a non-EU supplier is required to appoint a VAT representative established in Luxembourg (severe liability) unless OSS (non-union scheme) is used.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (1) Article 175bis LIR (Luxembourg Income Tax Law) election: an SCSp formed in Luxembourg may irrevocably opt to be treated as a taxable corporate entity (opaque status) for Luxembourg tax purposes, provided that, for the entire tax year, all partners are residents of Luxembourg or of a treaty state and are effectively taxable on their share of partnership profits in that state. (2) ATAD 2 reverse hybrid-mismatch sweep (art. 160ter LIR): where all the SCSp's participants are tax-resident outside Luxembourg and treat the entity as opaque, Luxembourg mandates entity-level taxation irrespective of the default transparency. (3) Partnership-level VAT unpredictability: transparency applies for income tax; for VAT the SCSp is, in practice, registered in its own name as the supplier of the esports platform services, with no election required. (4) No general 'check-the-box' classification regime exists under Luxembourg law comparable to the US federal check-the-box; the contrast between the default transparency and art. 175bis election reproduces the 'check-the-box' outcome flexibility for hybrid planning.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Luxembourg VAT law of 12 February 1979, as amended; alignment with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the Luxembourg small-business exemption applicable to established taxable persons selling primarily to final consumers; however, an SCSp or any supplier making taxable supplies of esports/digital platform services in Luxembourg must register from the first euro (no threshold) for mandatory AEDT registration, and non-established suppliers of B2C electronic services must register via OSS/Union scheme irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently impose real-time fiscal clearance, API transmission, or digital stamping. E-invoicing is permitted on a consensual basis (buyer's agreement required, art. 54(3) of the Luxembourg VAT Implementation Regulation). Luxembourg is committed to the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) roadmap, with mandatory structured e-invoicing (EU standard EN 16931 via Peppol) for intra-EU B2B supplies expected, at the earliest, in the 2030–2035 window; domestic B2G e-invoicing is facultative with the public buyer's acceptance. Until then, PDF/A or Peppol BIS quality XML invoices are accepted; no state-managed central exchange platform.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods outside the EU is zero-rated (art. 41 VAT Law) upon proof of shipment. Export of services (including esports platform/matchmaking, tournament SaaS, digital community subscriptions and hosting fees) is zero-rated (art. 44) when the business customer is established outside the EU or, for B2C digital services, when the recipient has his residence/usual residence outside the EU and the effective use and enjoyment test is satisfied; intra-EU B2B services fall under Luxembourg reverse charge. For B2C electronic services supplied intra-EU, the supply is taxed in the Member State of the consumer (via OSS) rather than zero-rated. Zero-rating requires contemporaneous evidence that the recipient has its seat/domicile outside the Union: VAT identification number (if any), IP geolocation logs, country metadata of the connected device, bank/BIC country of the payment instrument, billing address, and hotel-billing indicators.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (single administrative document / electronic export declaration through Luxembourg customs) where physical goods are exported from the EU
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing the physical dispatch of exported goods
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank statement or SWIFT/Stripe/PayPal payment records evidencing the receipt of the export consideration from the non-EU customer)
Signed master service/subscription contract documenting the non-EU recipient's establishment and the nature of the B2B supply
IP address geolocation and device metadata logs for B2C digital esports services, demonstrating placement of the consumer outside the EU
Foreign VAT ID certificate (VRN) or EU OSS records for intra-EU business customers
Annual EC Sales List / recapitulative statement and Intrastat filings in respect of intra-EU supplies

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks (ESCB); prudential regulation and supervision of credit institutions, payment institutions and electronic-money institutions are exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), with the BCL responsible for monetary policy operations and balance-of-payments statistics.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) is the domestic currency and is fully convertible. Luxembourg implements the EU free movement of capital regime under Article 63 TFEU and Directive 88/361/EEC; there are no exchange controls, no prior central-bank authorisation for inbound or outbound payments, and no restriction on profit or capital repatriation. The SCSp may receive and disburse partner contributions, prize pools, sponsorship revenue and commercial settlements freely in EUR or any foreign currency. Because the SCSp is fiscally transparent, partnership distributions are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax at entity level; treaty-based withholding analysis applies only to Luxembourg-source income of underlying companies, where the standard domestic rate of 15% on dividends may be reduced or eliminated under an applicable double-tax treaty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio and no repatriation period for export proceeds, platform fees, sponsorship or advertising revenue received in foreign currency. USD and other foreign-currency receipts may be retained in foreign-currency accounts, converted freely, or applied directly to obligations. The only compliance duty is statistical: resident entities must report qualifying cross-border transactions to the BCL for balance-of-payments and external-stocks statistics under the ECB statistics framework (ECB Regulation 2533/98), with no impact on treasury freedom.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account plus EUR/USD Operational Current Account with daily sweeping, cash-pooling and a contractual set-off waiver; account titled in the name of the SCSp acting by its General Partner.
Operational Corporate Account with SWIFT direct access, payment factory integration and dual-currency collections suitable for high-volume marketplace flows.
Operational Account for tournament settlement and sponsorship flows; transaction-banking desk experienced with partnership vehicles and regulated gaming-adjacent businesses.
Wealth-linked Partnership Account better suited to private-asset SCSp structures than to high-velocity esports transaction flows.
Digital Corporate Account with remote e-banking mandates and API connectivity; acceptable for low-to-mid volume treasury operations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as an auxiliary payment channel; not viable as a primary settlement bank. The SCSp may lawfully use EU-authorised Payment Institutions and Electronic Money Institutions passporting into Luxembourg under PSD2 (Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services, as amended) and the Law of 14 December 2001 on electronic money, as amended. The target payment rails are fully compliant: PayPal (Europe) S.a r.l. et Cie, S.C.A. is a Luxembourg-authorised credit institution supervised by the CSSF, and Stripe Payments Europe Ltd (Ireland) operates through EU passporting into Luxembourg. Unregulated offshore EMIs are prohibited: providing payment services or issuing e-money in Luxembourg without CSSF authorisation or a valid EU passport constitutes a criminal offence. Treasury policy: route all collections via Stripe/PayPal into a Tier-1 operational account with daily sweeps; do not warehouse balances with an EMI beyond contractual settlement windows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is legally permissible. The CSSF AML framework (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended) recognises video-identification and eIDAS-qualified electronic signatures as equivalent to physical presence. In practice, Tier-1 banks require one live video compliance interview with the authorised signatories of the General Partner; they do not require the SCSp partners to appear physically. A physical branch visit may be imposed only where video identification is inconclusive or where the principal's passport cannot be electronically verified. Documents executed abroad must be apostilled; if the General Partner is a corporate entity, a certificate of incumbency and a board resolution authorising account opening must accompany the application.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp transparency and absence of legal personality: banks cannot identify the legal account holder and fear hidden silent partners with undisclosed economic interests.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the partnership deed (contrat de société) filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS); RCS registration extract; legal opinion from Luxembourg counsel confirming the SCSp's valid existence, the General Partner's power to open and operate accounts on behalf of the SCSp, and the partners' liability profile; beneficial-ownership register identifying every partner holding 25% or more and all ultimate beneficial owners of the General Partner; passports, proof of address, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements for each identified person; signed account mandate listing only the authorised signatories; contractual set-off waiver protecting investor capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Esports tournament payments resemble gambling activity; rapid deposit-and-withdrawal cycles may trigger suspicious-transaction reporting for unlicensed gaming.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Regulatory characterisation memorandum confirming that skill-based esports competition is not gambling under the Luxembourg Law of 22 June 1963 on games of chance and that no gaming licence is required; tournament rules, scoring algorithms and prize-pool mechanics evidencing skill predominance; player age-verification and KYC logs; responsible-gaming and anti-fraud internal policies; transparent payment descriptions such as 'esports prize award' on all beneficiary credit lines; complete prize ledger keyed to unique tournament references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity cross-border micro-payments from Stripe/PayPal against a thin capital base create unusual transaction patterns and reverse-KYC concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited cash-flow narrative reconciling PSP settlement reports to the operational account; executed merchant agreements with Stripe and PayPal; sponsor contracts, player sign-on agreements and affiliate invoices; capital call notices and funding forecasts aligned to the partnership deed; API-driven or CSV-based transaction reporting feed enabling the bank to interrogate flow history in real time; confirmation that all PSP settlements are subject to daily sweeping into the Tier-1 account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: EU-resident partners inject EUR via SEPA Credit Transfer referencing the capital call number and the partnership deed date; the receiving bank requires a capital call notice, source-of-funds declaration and UBO confirmation and credits the dedicated Capital Escrow Account. Non-EU partners (including Chinese investors) route USD or EUR via SWIFT MT103 with a direct-investment purpose code; the remitting bank applies its home-country ODI/SAFE approval requirements, while the Luxembourg beneficiary bank requires the RCS extract, partnership deed, legal opinion and UBO documentation. Funds must match the capital call amount exactly to permit straightforward booking; any deviation is re-characterised as a shareholder loan and must be documented under a separate loan agreement. Short-term working capital may be advanced by the General Partner through a documented intra-group current account. No Luxembourg authorisation or BCL permit is required for any of these routes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail: SWIFT MT103 for cross-border supplier payments, sponsorship rebates and prize awards, with complete remittance information in field 70 (e.g., 'Esports prize award - [tournament code]' or 'Platform licence fee - [agreement reference]') to satisfy FATF Recommendation 16 and bank sanctions screening. EU-resident beneficiaries receive SEPA Instant or SEPA Credit Transfers with end-to-end references. Commercial letters of credit are not appropriate for services; an irrevocable confirmed LC would be reserved only for physical tournament hardware imports on seller insistence. Daily treasury sweeps consolidate Stripe/PayPal USD into EUR accounts at the Tier-1 bank, with same-day SEPA disbursements for player prizes and weekly batching of MT103s for non-EU counterparties.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable FX forwards (tenors 1-6 months) hedging the conversion of Stripe/PayPal USD settlement batches into EUR, executed under a standard ISDA master agreement or the bank's master forward contract
EUR/USD FX swaps to roll short-dated USD working capital without crystallising spot exposure
Deliverable EUR/CNY forwards to hedge flows with Chinese parent or sponsor counterparties if and when such flows materialise
Vanilla EUR/USD FX options (zero-premium collars) where the bank extends a commercial-risk hedging limit

Non-deliverable forwards are not recommended for EUR/USD because the onshore deliverable market is deep and liquid; NDFs would be relevant only for genuinely inconvertible settlement currencies (e.g., INR) which are outside the target payment rails; any FX derivative transaction requires an LEI for the SCSp and, where the clearing threshold is exceeded, EMIR central clearing and trade-repository reporting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (comptes annuels) or filing confirmation to the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 7 months after financial year-end (e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines up to EUR 5,000; additional administrative penalties up to EUR 10,000; repeated defaults can lead to judicial dissolution or RCS strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) – Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership; no fixed annual date, but annual internal verification is expected at the time of the annual accounts approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine from EUR 1,250 up to EUR 1,250,000 and/or imprisonment (6 months to 5 years); administrative fines of EUR 200 per day for non-update.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the SCSp exceeds two of the following three thresholds: total assets > EUR 4.4 million; net turnover > EUR 8.8 million; average staff > 50. Audit may also be required by the partnership agreement or upon a shareholder request under Luxembourg law.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (law of 19 December 2002) is the default; IFRS is permitted for non-listed entities and mandatory for listed entities. For a small SCSp, a simplified balance sheet may be prepared.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: SCSp is not required to file a standalone annual UBO confirmation. However, the RBE records must be updated within 30 days of any shareholding transfer or other change. An annual review of the RBE file, carried out jointly with the annual accounts approval, should confirm the information is current; if no changes occurred, no update filing is made.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – USD 25,000 for a statutory audit; if exemption applies, USD 2,000 – USD 5,000 for a review or compilation

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Luxembourg SCSp is fiscally transparent; no CIT at entity level. Each partner is taxed on their share of income. The IP Tax Regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income) and the Luxembourg R&D tax credit may apply to eligible corporate partners. Municipal business tax (6.75%-10.5%) and contribution to the Employment Fund (0.7%) are integrated in the headline CIT rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate income tax return Form 561 (Formulaire 561) and municipal business tax return Form 561/CC; filed via the MyGuichet.lu electronic filing portal (e-TVA/e-filing service).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year-end: 31 December. Return must be filed and tax paid by 31 March of the following year; extension to 30 June available upon request. For fiscal years ending 31 December 2024 and 2025, the deadline is extended to 31 December 2025 and 31 December 2026 respectively under the COVID-19 administrative deferral practice; standard deadline is otherwise strictly enforced.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership name, legal form, RCS registration number, registered office address, fiscal year dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate SCSp as fiscally transparent and provide in the annex the complete partner schedule (name, address, tax residence, share of profits) and each partner's Luxembourg tax number if applicable; non-resident partners must not file a Luxembourg return solely on this basis unless locally taxable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit and loss summary, including gross income, operational expenses, financial income, and exceptional items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Luxembourg-source income attributable to the SCSp allocated to non-resident partners. Esports platform fees, tournament entry fees, advertising, and sponsorship income sourced in Luxembourg must be allocated per the partnership agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions, tax losses brought forward, and IP regime exemption (80% deduction on qualifying IP income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the IP regime only where the demerged partner is a Luxembourg CIT taxpayer and holds the qualifying IP; non-resident partners cannot claim this exemption on their share unless a permanent establishment in Luxembourg exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments to accounting profit to obtain taxable income, including disallowed expenses and allocation to partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: SCSp must attach the partner allocation statement showing each non-resident partner's distributive share of Luxembourg-source income, using the arm's length allocation basis per the partnership agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: For transparent entities, only individual corporate partners' taxable wealth base is reported; SCSp own filing requires the annual net wealth tax return only if the partnership is not considered fully transparent for NWT purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners holding the SCSp interest through a Luxembourg establishment are subject to net wealth tax on the proportionate taxable value; otherwise ignore.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: EUR 100 per month per taxable period, capped at EUR 5,000. Additional late payment interest at 0.6% per month on unpaid tax amounts. If tax is effectively assessed at a higher amount than declared, a 10% penalty applies on the tax underpayment. VAT penalties apply separately if e-commerce reverse-charge or platform ordering transactions are treated incorrectly.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg dividend withholding tax (WHT) for distributions from a Luxembourg corporate resident. No WHT applies on distributions of profits by an SCSp because the SCSp is fiscally transparent; the underlying corporate entity holding shares in an operating affiliate, if any, would trigger WHT at 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner must submit a Luxembourg self-issued tax residence certificate (Formulaire 100) or a foreign equivalent, complete the Luxembourg WHT exemption/refund form (Form 112/105), and file the application with the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (Luxembourg Inland Revenue, Administration des contributions directes). Reduced rates apply under Luxembourg's DTA network (e.g., 0% or 5% for substantial shareholdings in certain treaties). The SCSp must ensure the recipient partner is the registered beneficial owner and hold the partnership agreement, residence certificate, and share register to evidence no artificial conduit arrangement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory WHT 15% for outbound royalties paid by a Luxembourg resident entity; most treaties reduce to 0-5%. Interest: statutory WHT 15%; treaty rates generally 0-10%; Luxembourg does not levy WHT on certain cross-border interest if the beneficial owner is an EU company under the Interest and Royalties Directive (2003/49/EC). For SCSp, payment flows to partners are characterized as profit shares, not royalties or interest, unless a separate debt/licence exists.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 3,000,000 aggregate related-party transactions requiring Local File preparation; Master File required if the group consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 50,000,000 and group related-party transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000. Although the SCSp is transparent, partners' controlled transactions with the platform are subject to Luxembourg transfer pricing documentation rules where the SCSp is the tested party.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance Requirements (ESR) under the OECD BEPS Action 5 and the EU ATAD. The SCSp must demonstrate real economic substance: its registered office in Luxembourg, local accounting records, central management and control, a minimum level of staff and operational expenditure for the esports platform activity, and performance of core income-generating activities in Luxembourg. For pure holding and financing transparent vehicles, a substance-to-risk ratio test applies, but for the esports community platform, genuine operational presence is required; failure leads to lack of substance presumption and potential recharacterization of profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (Luxembourg Criminal Code Art. 396 and General Tax Law §396)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful failure to declare the SCSp's Luxembourg-source esports revenue, concealment of partner profit shares, use of falsified financial records, or deliberate mispricing of tournament fees and advertisement income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine from EUR 10,000 to EUR 1,000,000, plus imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years for directors or managers; full restitution of evaded taxes and automatic penalties up to 100% of the underdeclared tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the SCSp general partner (personne responsable) are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they knowingly caused non-payment; travel bans, seizure of personal assets, and extradition procedures apply under mutual assistance agreements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp as a front for another group entity with no real presence, no decision-making activity, no adequate staffing, or entering into circular transactions to attract unjustified treaty benefits or to misclassify profits as transparent distributions to avoid Luxembourg taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the SCSp as fully taxable, reassessment of profits at the entity level, 10% delinquency penalty, interest at 0.6% per month, and refusal of tax treaty benefits (e.g., under the Principal Purpose Test).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners and directors become personally liable for the entire reassessed tax if the corporate veil is pierced; the Luxembourg Commercial Court may order claw-back of distributions and disqualification from serving as director for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT and VASP/Esports Payment Processing Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Stripe or PayPal as payment rails without conducting customer due diligence, anti-money-laundering registration under the Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004, or ignoring transaction monitoring obligations for prize payouts and user-to-user transfers on the esports platform.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine up to EUR 1,250,000 or 10% of annual turnover for serious breaches; criminal sanctions for failure to report suspicious transactions, and revocation of the Luxembourg operating license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Compliance officers and directors may face criminal liability including imprisonment up to 5 years and personal fines; travel bans and asset freezes for serious AML failures under CSSF enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Substance Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare, maintain, or file the statutory transfer pricing documentation (Local File) or the CbCR schedule when the platform's intra-group transactions exceed the EUR 3,000,000 threshold, or applying non-arm's-length royalty payments to a foreign related partner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of EUR 5,000 per missing or incomplete document; upward TP adjustment with 10% reassessment surcharge and 0.6% monthly interest; autonomous penalty of up to EUR 250,000 for material non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the SCSp manager who signed false declarations are personally liable for the resulting tax deficiencies; the Luxembourg Tax Administration can seek attachment of personal bank accounts and real estate.
